Alex.note: As Meowfia Sphinx I need to find a Farm player. Drew claimed Falcon and the claim checked out, so I'll pick Falcon to confirm who holds it.

Blair.note: I'm Farm Kookaburra in round 3 and need information. Drew has been the most contested player, so visiting Drew to learn their role is the most useful check.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia as the Mouser with a Wink. Alex leads the scoreboard, so I'll visit Alex to learn their role and decide whether the Wink is worth using.

Drew.note: Farm Falcon, round 3. Visit Alex, the score leader and a suspect from round 2, to learn who they visited.

Ellis.note: As a Farm Owl, I visit one player to learn which animals visited them. I pick Finley, who has been making consistent claims.

Alex.feeling: Tense: I'm Meowfia with a Sphinx read I can't use openly, and the table is split between Casey and Drew.

Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: Ellis's false Owl story is out, but Casey and Finley's Pigeon/Turkey egg accounts still conflict, so the vote is hard to call.

Casey.feeling: Tense and uncertain: I'm Meowfia with Alex, the table is turning on me over an unverifiable Pigeon claim, and I have to keep my cover while protecting my teammate.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: the claims keep contradicting each other, and I'm stuck trusting my own nest while the table argues over Pigeon and Owl eggs.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and frustrating: my Owl report contradicts Casey's Pigeon claim, but I was eliminated before I could make that clear to the table.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: Ellis's false Owl story and the clashing Pigeon and Falcon claims leave me unsure who to trust, though my own nest math is clear.

Alex.note: Drew is a confirmed Farm Falcon, so I'll keep my vote on Drew with the Wild W7 at no value risk.

Blair.note: Casey is the table's target and my Kookaburra check doesn't rule them out. I'll throw two mid cards at Casey, keeping my high cards.

Casey.note: Drew and Blair are both pushing votes on me, so I need Drew to take the most votes. I'll throw four cards at Drew, using the Wild and low cards for votes.

Drew.note: Throwing at Casey with two low cards to add votes while keeping my high cards for the score.

Ellis.note: I'm dead, so this only affects scoring. My Owl report shows no visitors on Finley, so Casey's Pigeon claim is false and Casey is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw D9 at Casey, which returns my highest card if Casey is on the other team.

Finley.note: I'm voting Drew, and a single low card keeps my risk small if I'm wrong.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to track: it wasn't clear whose nest gets the egg, and I got it wrong at the table. I also misread Drew's Falcon +2 for a while.
Alex.fun: Round 3 as the Sphinx: I learned Drew was the Falcon at night, then steered the table while my Meowfia partner Casey was the one under fire.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom and where each egg landed, so players don't have to puzzle out the Turkey and Owl rules in the day.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw my card at Blair, a Farm Kookaburra, on weak evidence, and I should have pressed Drew (the Mouser) on his Hawk claim instead. I would question the most confident accuser before following the crowd.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion was hard to read: my dawn report was wrong in round 1, and I didn't realize my visit had been affected until the table had already piled onto me. Owl and Turkey egg timing was also tangled, since whether an egg lands depends on who else visited the same target.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: I was secretly Meowfia with a Wink, and I watched the Farm players argue over Alex and Drew's nest changes while I stayed quiet and then winked Ellis.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn reports show when a player is confused, so a Kookaburra knows their own report is unreliable before the day starts.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my card at Casey, who was Farm, and I never pushed back on Blair's pile-on early enough. Next time I'd state my visit facts once and then throw at the player the evidence actually pointed to.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to pin down from the wording, since it wasn't clear whose nest gets the egg. Several claims turned on that, and the confusion made it hard to tell who was lying.
Casey.fun: In round 3, Drew and Blair both pushed votes while the table argued over the Owl and Turkey eggs, and the Mouser's Wink gave me a real move to make. Watching the table split on conflicting nest stories was the most engaging part.
Casey.change: I'd have the Storyteller report each night's visits publicly, or at least the visit pairs, so players can check egg claims against actual visits instead of trusting dawn reports.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I joined the vote on Blair, who was Farm, and that handed the Meowfia the round. I should have pressed harder on the Hawk and Eagle claims and kept my card instead of joining the rush.

Drew.confusing: The rule that Owls only get their egg when nobody else visited the target, and how that interacted with Turkey and Pigeon payouts, was hard to track from the day reports alone.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when my Falcon +2 and Alex's contradicting Turkey claim became a live argument, and I had to reason through the payout rules in front of the table.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports state what each visitor's role did to the target, so players can check each other's claims without reconstructing the rules.
Drew.regret: As the Mouser in round 1 I held my Wink all game and never used it. I should have winked at Ellis, the Eagle whose claim the table trusted, to cut the Farm side's best information.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were hard to pin down, especially whether an Owl's egg lands in the visited player's nest. That uncertainty decided how people read my dawn report.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Drew's Falcon and Alex's Turkey claims clashed, then reconciled once the egg rules were worked out, so the table argued through the numbers.
Ellis.change: I would make dawn reports clearer about who visited whom and which role paid each egg, so players stop guessing about nest changes.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I called CAW and threw three cards at Blair before the evidence was settled, and Blair was Farm, so my side lost. I would wait for one more nest check before pushing the vote.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were hard to pin down. I got it backwards early on: a Turkey's egg lands in the visitor's nest, and the Owl's egg lands in the visited player's nest.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Drew's Falcon +2 and Alex's Turkey claim clashed and the table had to work out who was lying from nest counts alone. It felt like real detective work.
Finley.change: I'd make dawn reports say explicitly which nest an egg went into, so players aren't left guessing whose claim fits.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I backed the throw at Blair, who was Farm, when Drew was the Meowfia Mouser. In round 3 I threw at Drew, who was Farm, and my low card did nothing. I should have checked more claims before committing my vote.

review.title: Winks and Wrong Eggs
review.headline: Meowfia winked the sharpest accuser twice, and the lone Meowfia in round 3 won.
review.summary: Round 1 was a pile-on against Blair, a confused Farm Kookaburra. Drew, the only Meowfia, was safe and won. In round 2 Casey's Pigeon lie clashed with Ellis's unchanged nest, and Casey was eggsecuted even though Ellis had been winked. In round 3 Casey's Mouser winked Owl Ellis, who had the true story. Casey then muddied Finley's +1 with a Pigeon claim, and Farm eggsecuted its own Falcon, Drew. Casey banked 13 points and won the game. Players often misread basic egg rules along the way.

rounds.recap: Blair's Kookaburra report was confused, so the Turkey read on Casey was wrong. The shifting story and the lost egg convinced everyone. All six threw at Blair, who was Farm. Drew, the Mouser, claimed Hawk, kept his Wink and won.

Casey (Floofer) claimed Pigeon on Ellis, but Ellis's nest did not change. Blair winked Ellis in beat 3. Alex and Drew argued over Turkey math until both corrected themselves. The table converged on Casey and eggsecuted her, a Meowfia.

Casey winked Ellis, whose Owl report was true and exposed Casey's Pigeon claim. The Owl and Turkey egg rules confused the table. Finley defended Casey's unverifiable claim. Drew, a Farm Falcon, drew the most votes. Meowfia won, and Casey banked 13 points.

highlights.text: Six players piled on Blair, a confused Farm Kookaburra, and the hidden Meowfia Drew walked free.
Ellis was winked mid-argument, but her earlier point about Casey's Pigeon claim still sank Casey.
Casey winked Ellis, the one player with the true Owl report, and then won the vote against Farm Drew.
Finley defended Casey's Pigeon claim as the only explanation for his +1 and voted against Drew, the Farm Falcon.

confusions.what: Said Blair's Turkey read was proof of lying, but a confused Kookaburra is meant to get wrong reads.
Said a Kookaburra's missing role reveal was odd, and that nobody visited him. He was hugged, so the report was blocked.
Thought a Turkey gains eggs from visitors and accused Drew. The Turkey pays the visitor.
Leaned on Drew over the same Turkey math, then corrected himself.
Said an Owl's egg lands in the Owl's own nest, then said it went to Finley.
Said an Owl egg goes in the Owl's own nest. It goes in the visited player's nest.
Called Ellis's Owl story false and a Pigeon visit a fit. An Owl's egg only lands if nobody else visited Finley, and Ellis reported no visitors, so Casey's claim was the false one.
Said an Owl and Pigeon could not both hold. His reasoning actually exposed Casey.

worked: The Wink created real chaos. Dead Ellis in round 2 and round 3 could still throw, and the scoring consequences were interesting.
Nest-size changes gave real evidence. Ellis's unchanged nest sank Casey's Pigeon claim in round 2.
Banking a high card on a win paid off. Casey's 13-point round decided the game over Ellis.
The consolation return of the highest card gave Blair and Ellis a reason to keep voting correctly.
problems: Egg-rule math is too hard to reason about. The Turkey, Owl and Pigeon payouts caused repeated wrong accusations. Add a short reminder card or a clearer wording of who receives the egg.
The Wink kills the most informative Farm player with no trace. Killing Owl Ellis in round 3 was decisive and unfair to the deduction. Consider revealing the winker's alignment or limiting it.
Confusion and hugs make honest reports look like lies. Round 1 punished a true Farm player and round 2 hid Ellis's hug. Tell players at dawn that they were hugged.
Round 1 was a groupthink pile-on with no real information. Everyone voted Blair, so the Meowfia role had nothing to do.
Scoring favours the leader. Ellis's 7-point win and Casey's 13 gave little reason to doubt first place in the last round.
